uncited: They differ from their siblings, such as [Spherical Harmonics Approximation](8741-spherical-harmonics-approximation.md) and [Volumetric Spherical Harmonics Precomputed Radiance Transfer](5807-volumetric-spherical-harmonics-precomputed-radiance-transfer.md), by defining the fundamental mathematical basis itself, whereas the siblings focus on specific application pipelines or optimization techniques built upon this basis.
A directional signal $f(\omega)$ is represented by a finite set of coefficients $\mathbf{f}$ of size $n = (L+1)^2$, where $L$ is the maximum degree (bandwidth) [Child 10564].
The linear index $i$ maps the degree $l$ and order $m$ via $i = l^2 + l + m$ [Child 10564].
